El evento de 248 keV en LZ y la búsqueda: The 248 keV event in LZ and the search for WIMPs
En esta charla nos centraremos en el eve: This talk focuses on the high-energy event recently observed by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) collaboration, presented in arXiv:2609.02823. We will use this result as a starting point to introduce how interactions between WIMPs and nuclei can be described using an effective field theory. We will then discuss the operation and calibration of the LZ experiment, as well as the reconstruction of the observed event. Finally, we will review the data analysis, its main background sources, and what conclusions can be drawn about the possible nature of this event.
¿Cómo se ve el universo cuando la luz no: What does the universe look like when light is not enough?
La luz ha sido nuestra principal herrami: Light has been our main tool for observing the Universe, but it cannot show us everything. Gravitational waves open a new observational window, allowing us to study extreme phenomena and explore epochs of the Universe that are inaccessible through electromagnetic radiation. In this talk, we will explore what gravitational waves are, how we detect them, and what they can tell us about the Universe, from collisions of compact objects to its earliest moments.
